Generated Narrative: CodeSystem fhir4eyes-cs

This case-sensitive code system https://YasniiSS.github.io/fhir4eyes/CodeSystem/fhir4eyes-cs defines the following codes:

CodeDisplayDefinition
central-corneal-thickness Central corneal thicknessCentral corneal thickness, independent of the eye measured. Eye-specific LOINC: 79825-6 (right) / 79826-4 (left).
specular-microscopy-panel Corneal endothelial specular microscopyPanel code for a corneal endothelial specular microscopy exam.
specular-capture-position Specular microscopy capture positionLocation of the corneal capture (central, paracentral, peripheral).
specular-analysis-method Specular microscopy analysis methodType of analysis method. Eye-specific LOINC: 100086-8 (right) / 100155-1 (left).
endothelial-cell-density Corneal endothelial cell densityEye-specific LOINC: 100070-2 (right) / 100071-0 (left).
endothelial-cells-counted Corneal endothelial cells countedEye-specific LOINC: 100076-9 (right) / 100077-7 (left).
endothelial-cell-area-cv Corneal endothelial cell area coefficient of variationEye-specific LOINC: 100072-8 (right) / 100073-6 (left).
endothelial-hexagonality Corneal endothelial hexagonalityEye-specific LOINC: 100074-4 (right) / 100075-1 (left).
endothelial-cell-area-min Corneal endothelial cell area, minimumEye-specific LOINC: 100078-5 (right) / 100079-3 (left).
endothelial-cell-area-max Corneal endothelial cell area, maximumEye-specific LOINC: 100080-1 (right) / 100081-9 (left).
endothelial-cell-area-mean Corneal endothelial cell area, meanEye-specific LOINC: 100082-7 (right) / 100083-5 (left).
endothelial-cell-area-sd Corneal endothelial cell area, standard deviationEye-specific LOINC: 100084-3 (right) / 100085-0 (left).
axial-length Axial lengthAnteroposterior length of the eye (corneal vertex to retina/RPE), e.g. by optical or ultrasound biometry.
anterior-chamber-depth Anterior chamber depthDistance from the cornea to the anterior lens surface.
lens-thickness Lens thicknessAxial thickness of the crystalline lens.
white-to-white White-to-white corneal diameterHorizontal visible corneal diameter (limbus to limbus).
keratometry-k1 Keratometry K1 (flat)Corneal power of the flattest meridian of the anterior corneal surface, in dioptres.
keratometry-k2 Keratometry K2 (steep)Corneal power of the steepest meridian of the anterior corneal surface, in dioptres.
keratometry-k1-radius Keratometry K1 radius of curvatureRadius of curvature of the flattest meridian of the anterior corneal surface, in millimetres.
keratometry-k2-radius Keratometry K2 radius of curvatureRadius of curvature of the steepest meridian of the anterior corneal surface, in millimetres.
corneal-astigmatism Corneal astigmatism (cylinder)Corneal (keratometric) astigmatism, the difference between steep and flat meridian powers (K2 - K1) in dioptres, reported as a positive magnitude (plus-cylinder notation) at the steep meridian.
keratometric-index Keratometric indexRefractive index used to convert corneal radius of curvature into corneal power (e.g. 1.3375).
pupil-diameter Pupil diameterDiameter of the pupil at the time of the measurement.
pupil-dilated Pupil dilatedWhether the pupil was pharmacologically dilated at the time of the measurement.
mydriatic-agent Mydriatic agentMydriatic agent used to dilate the pupil, if any.
test-distance Testing distanceDistance between the patient and the test target (chart, fixation target) during the test, as a measured quantity. For a near/far category use test-distance-category.
correction-status Refractive correction status during testWhether the test was performed with or without the patient's refractive correction.
ocular-biometry Ocular biometryPanel code for an ocular biometry exam (optical or ultrasound), typically for IOL power calculation. Formula results are separate IOL formula result observations.
axial-length-measurement-type Axial length measurement typeTechnique used to measure axial length: optical, ultrasound immersion or ultrasound contact.
axial-length-snr Axial length signal-to-noise ratioSignal-to-noise ratio of the optical axial length measurement, a quality indicator.
axial-length-selection-method Axial length selection methodMethod used to select the reported axial length from multiple measurements.
anterior-chamber-depth-definition Anterior chamber depth definitionReference surfaces used for the ACD measurement (corneal epithelium or endothelium to anterior lens).
lens-status Lens statusStatus of the crystalline lens: phakic, pseudophakic or aphakic.
vitreous-status Vitreous statusStatus of the vitreous body, relevant to the sound velocity used in ultrasound biometry.
keratometry-mean-radius Keratometry mean radius of curvature (R/SE)Mean radius of curvature of the anterior corneal surface in mm, (K1 radius + K2 radius)/2, as reported in the R part of the biometer R/SE field. The dioptric mean (SE) is keratometry-km.
refractive-surgery-history Refractive surgery historyPrior corneal or refractive surgery of the eye, critical for IOL formula selection.
target-refraction Target refractionDesired postoperative refraction used for IOL power calculation.
refractive-error-type Refractive error typeType of refractive error of the eye.
measurement-data-source Measurement data sourceOrigin of the biometry measurement data (e.g. automatic, manually entered, from another device).
vertex-distance Vertex distanceDistance between the back surface of a spectacle lens and the corneal apex.
iol-formula-result IOL power calculation formula resultPanel code for the result of one IOL power calculation formula applied to an ocular biometry exam.
iol-formula IOL power calculation formulaFormula used for the IOL power calculation (e.g. Barrett Universal II, SRK/T, Holladay 2, Kane).
iol-lens-constant-type IOL lens constant typeType of IOL optimization constant (e.g. A-constant, surgeon factor, ACD constant).
iol-lens-constant-value IOL lens constant valueValue of the IOL optimization constant used for the calculation.
iol-model Suggested IOL modelIntraocular lens model suggested by this formula calculation.
iol-power Recommended IOL powerIOL power, in dioptres, recommended by this formula calculation.
iol-expected-refraction Predicted postoperative refractionRefraction predicted by the formula for the recommended IOL power.
iol-power-table IOL power tableRange of IOL powers with the predicted refraction for each, as listed in the biometry report for this formula.
visual-acuity-scale Visual acuity notation scaleNotation in which the visual acuity value is expressed (e.g. Snellen fraction, decimal, LogMAR).
pinhole-used Pinhole occluder usedWhether the visual acuity measurement was taken through a pinhole occluder.
corrected-intraocular-pressure Intraocular pressure corrected for central corneal thicknessIntraocular pressure adjusted for central corneal thickness, derived from an IOP reading and a pachymetry measurement. LOINC 96093-0/96092-2 (compensated IOP) exist but may not be equivalent to CCT-based correction; not used.
tension-curve Diurnal intraocular pressure tension curvePanel grouping several intraocular pressure readings taken across a single day (diurnal / ambulatory tension curve).
corneal-tomography-anterior-surface Corneal tomography, anterior surface analysisAnterior corneal surface analysis component of a corneal tomography exam.
keratometry-kmax Maximum keratometry (Kmax)Maximum keratometric power on the anterior corneal surface; key parameter for keratoconus detection and progression.
simulated-keratometry Simulated keratometry (SimK)Simulated keratometry values (steep/flat) derived from the topographic/tomographic map.
corneal-radius-horizontal Horizontal corneal radius of curvature (Rh)Corneal radius of curvature along the horizontal (0-180 degree) meridian; not necessarily a principal (K1/K2) meridian.
corneal-radius-vertical Vertical corneal radius of curvature (Rv)Corneal radius of curvature along the vertical (90 degree) meridian; not necessarily a principal (K1/K2) meridian.
corneal-asphericity-q-anterior Corneal asphericity (Q-value), anterior surfaceAsphericity (Q-value) of the anterior corneal surface; typical normal value about -0.26.
elevation-anterior Corneal elevation relative to best fit sphere, anterior surfaceElevation of the anterior corneal surface relative to its best fit sphere.
best-fit-sphere-radius-anterior Best fit sphere radius, anterior surfaceRadius of the best fit sphere of the anterior corneal surface.
surface-regularity-index Surface Regularity Index (SRI)Topographic index of local corneal surface regularity within the central zone.
surface-asymmetry-index Surface Asymmetry Index (SAI)Topographic index of corneal power asymmetry between opposite hemimeridians.
inferior-superior-asymmetry Inferior-superior asymmetry value (I-S)Difference in mean corneal power between inferior and superior regions; keratoconus screening value.
kisa-index KISA% indexKISA% keratoconus screening index combining central K, I-S value, astigmatism and skewed radial axis.
topographic-pattern Topographic patternClassification of the corneal topographic map pattern (regular, irregular, keratoconus, pellucid, post-LASIK, forme fruste).
total-corneal-refractive-power Total corneal refractive power (TCRP)Total corneal refractive power calculated by ray tracing through anterior and posterior corneal surfaces.
true-net-power True net corneal power (TNP)True net corneal power calculated from anterior and posterior corneal curvature using Gaussian optics.
equivalent-keratometry-1mm Equivalent K reading (EKR), 1.0 mm zoneHolladay equivalent keratometry reading over a 1.0 mm zone.
equivalent-keratometry-3mm Equivalent K reading (EKR), 3.0 mm zoneHolladay equivalent keratometry reading over a 3.0 mm zone.
equivalent-keratometry-4-5mm Equivalent K reading (EKR), 4.5 mm zoneHolladay equivalent keratometry reading over a 4.5 mm zone; used for IOL calculation after refractive surgery.
corneal-mean-power-3mm-zone Mean corneal power, 3 mm zoneMean corneal power within the central 3 mm zone.
corneal-astigmatism-power-3mm-zone Corneal astigmatism power, 3 mm zoneCorneal astigmatism power within the central 3 mm zone.
corneal-steep-axis-3mm-zone Corneal steep axis, 3 mm zoneSteep meridian axis within the central 3 mm zone.
corneal-flat-axis-3mm-zone Corneal flat axis, 3 mm zoneFlat meridian axis within the central 3 mm zone.
corneal-mean-power-5mm-zone Mean corneal power, 5 mm zoneMean corneal power within the central 5 mm zone.
corneal-astigmatism-power-5mm-zone Corneal astigmatism power, 5 mm zoneCorneal astigmatism power within the central 5 mm zone.
corneal-steep-axis-5mm-zone Corneal steep axis, 5 mm zoneSteep meridian axis within the central 5 mm zone.
corneal-flat-axis-5mm-zone Corneal flat axis, 5 mm zoneFlat meridian axis within the central 5 mm zone.
total-corneal-astigmatism Total corneal astigmatism (tWFA)Total corneal astigmatism including the posterior surface, derived from corneal wavefront analysis.
corneal-irregular-astigmatism Total corneal irregular astigmatismHigher-order (irregular) component of total corneal astigmatism.
corneal-hoa-rms Corneal higher-order aberrations RMSRoot mean square of corneal higher-order wavefront aberrations.
angle-kappa Angle kappaAngle between the visual axis and the pupillary axis.
angle-kappa-intercept Angle kappa interceptCoordinates (x,y) of the angle kappa intercept relative to the pupil centre.
surgically-induced-astigmatism Surgically induced astigmatism (SIA)Expected corneal astigmatism induced by the surgical incision, used in surgical planning.
predicted-postoperative-corneal-astigmatism Predicted postoperative corneal astigmatismExpected residual corneal astigmatism after surgery, used in toric IOL planning.
toric-iol-optimal-axis Optimal toric IOL axisRecommended implantation axis for a toric intraocular lens.
corneal-vertex-location Corneal vertex locationPosition coordinates of the corneal vertex.
pupil-centroid-x Pupil centroid X coordinateX-coordinate of the pupil centre.
pupil-centroid-y Pupil centroid Y coordinateY-coordinate of the pupil centre.
equivalent-pupil-radius Equivalent pupil radiusRadius of the equivalent circular pupil.
corneal-topography-map-type Corneal topography map typeType of topographic map encoded (axial, tangential, elevation, refractive, pachymetry).
corneal-analyzed-area Corneal analyzed areaTotal area of the cornea analyzed.
corneal-eccentricity-index Corneal eccentricity indexCorneal eccentricity (shape factor).
keratoconus-prediction-index Keratoconus prediction index (KPI)Corneal keratoconus prediction index, distinct from KISA%.
potential-visual-acuity-decimal Decimal potential visual acuityEstimated potential visual acuity (decimal) from the corneal surface.
corneal-tomography-posterior-surface Corneal tomography, posterior surface analysisPosterior corneal surface analysis component of a corneal tomography exam.
posterior-keratometry-k1 Posterior keratometry K1 (flat)Keratometric power of the flattest meridian of the posterior corneal surface; a negative value in dioptres.
posterior-keratometry-k2 Posterior keratometry K2 (steep)Keratometric power of the steepest meridian of the posterior corneal surface; a negative value in dioptres.
posterior-keratometry-km Posterior keratometry Km (mean)Mean keratometric power of the posterior corneal surface; a negative value in dioptres.
corneal-astigmatism-posterior Corneal astigmatism, posterior surfaceAstigmatism of the posterior corneal surface, reported as a positive magnitude in dioptres (difference between posterior K2 and K1) with the posterior steep meridian as axis.
corneal-asphericity-q-posterior Corneal asphericity (Q-value), posterior surfaceAsphericity (Q-value) of the posterior corneal surface.
elevation-posterior Corneal elevation relative to best fit sphere, posterior surfaceElevation of the posterior corneal surface relative to its best fit sphere.
best-fit-sphere-radius-posterior Best fit sphere radius, posterior surfaceRadius of the best fit sphere of the posterior corneal surface.
corneal-tomography-pachymetry Corneal tomography, pachymetry analysisPachymetry (corneal thickness map) component of a corneal tomography exam.
corneal-thickness-pupil-centre Corneal thickness at pupil centreCorneal thickness measured at the pupil centre; may differ from the thickness at the corneal apex.
corneal-thickness-thinnest Thinnest corneal thicknessCorneal thickness at the thinnest point of the pachymetry map.
corneal-thinnest-point-location Thinnest corneal point locationLocation (x,y) of the thinnest corneal point relative to the reference centre.
corneal-volume Corneal volumeTotal corneal volume within the analysed diameter.
corneal-tomography-anterior-chamber Corneal tomography, anterior chamber analysisAnterior chamber analysis component of a corneal tomography exam.
anterior-chamber-volume Anterior chamber volumeVolume of the anterior chamber.
anterior-chamber-angle Anterior chamber angleIridocorneal (anterior chamber) angle width in degrees, as measured by the tomographer.
keratoconus-indices Keratoconus indicesKeratoconus screening and classification indices component of a corneal tomography exam.
bad-d Belin-Ambrosio total deviation (BAD-D)Final overall deviation index (D) of the Belin-Ambrosio Enhanced Ectasia Display; key keratoconus screening index.
bad-df Belin-Ambrosio front elevation deviation (Df)Deviation of anterior elevation relative to the enhanced best fit sphere (BAD component Df).
bad-db Belin-Ambrosio back elevation deviation (Db)Deviation of posterior elevation relative to the enhanced best fit sphere (BAD component Db).
bad-dt Belin-Ambrosio thinnest point deviation (Dt)Deviation of the thinnest corneal thickness from normal (BAD component Dt).
bad-dy Belin-Ambrosio vertical asymmetry deviation (Dy)Deviation of the Y-coordinate (vertical displacement) of the thinnest point (BAD component Dy).
bad-classification Belin-Ambrosio classificationClassification of the Belin-Ambrosio display result (normal, suspicious, abnormal).
enhanced-best-fit-sphere-radius-anterior Enhanced best fit sphere radius, anterior surfaceRadius of the enhanced best fit sphere of the anterior corneal surface (BAD enhanced reference).
enhanced-best-fit-sphere-radius-posterior Enhanced best fit sphere radius, posterior surfaceRadius of the enhanced best fit sphere of the posterior corneal surface (BAD enhanced reference).
amsler-krumeich-stage Amsler-Krumeich keratoconus stageClassic Amsler-Krumeich keratoconus staging (I-IV).
belin-abcd-grade Belin ABCD keratoconus gradeBelin ABCD keratoconus grading (anterior and posterior radius of curvature, thinnest pachymetry, distance visual acuity).
index-surface-variance Index of surface variance (ISV)Topometric index of the deviation of individual corneal radii from the mean.
index-vertical-asymmetry Index of vertical asymmetry (IVA)Topometric index of superior-inferior corneal curvature asymmetry.
keratoconus-index Keratoconus index (KI)Topometric ratio of central to peripheral corneal curvature.
center-keratoconus-index Center keratoconus index (CKI)Topometric central corneal curvature index.
index-height-asymmetry Index of height asymmetry (IHA)Topometric index of superior-inferior corneal elevation asymmetry.
index-height-decentration Index of height decentration (IHD)Topometric index of the degree of vertical decentration of corneal elevation.
topographic-keratoconus-classification Topographic keratoconus classification (TKC)Automated topographic keratoconus classification provided by the tomographer.
corneal-densitometry Corneal densitometryCorneal densitometry (light backscatter) component of a corneal tomography exam.
corneal-densitometry-zone-0-2mm Corneal densitometry, 0-2 mm zoneCorneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) in the central 0-2 mm annular zone.
corneal-densitometry-zone-2-6mm Corneal densitometry, 2-6 mm zoneCorneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) in the paracentral 2-6 mm annular zone.
corneal-densitometry-zone-6-10mm Corneal densitometry, 6-10 mm zoneCorneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) in the peripheral 6-10 mm annular zone.
corneal-densitometry-total Corneal densitometry, totalOverall corneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units).
corneal-densitometry-anterior-layer Corneal densitometry, anterior layerCorneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) of the anterior 120 um layer.
corneal-densitometry-central-layer Corneal densitometry, central layerCorneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) of the central stromal layer.
corneal-densitometry-posterior-layer Corneal densitometry, posterior layerCorneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) of the posterior 60 um layer.
keratometry-k1-axis Keratometry K1 axisOrientation of the flat meridian.
keratometry-k2-axis Keratometry K2 axisOrientation of the steep meridian.
keratometry-km Keratometry Km (mean)Mean keratometry, (K1+K2)/2.
pachymetric-progression Pachymetric progression index (BAD Dp)Rate of corneal thickness increase from the thinnest point toward the periphery; the pachymetric progression deviation (Dp) of the Belin-Ambrosio display.
radius-minimum-curvature Minimum radius of curvature (Rmin)Radius of curvature at the steepest point of the corneal surface.
radius-minimum-sagittal Minimum sagittal radius of curvature (Rmin)Minimum radius of sagittal (axial) curvature, i.e. the steepest point of the sagittal curvature map (Pentacam topometric index Rmin).
signal-strength Scan signal strength / qualityDevice-reported scan signal strength or quality score.
retinal-thickness-definition Retinal thickness definitionBoundaries used to define a retinal or RNFL thickness measurement (e.g. ILM to RPE, ILM to Bruch's membrane, ILM to RNFL outer boundary).
normative-deviation-category Normative database deviation categoryClassification of a measurement against the device normative database (e.g. within normal limits, borderline, outside normal limits).
pupil-dilation-degree Degree of pupil dilationDegree of pupil dilation, expressed as pupil diameter in mm.
central-subfield-thickness-min Central subfield thickness, minimumMinimum retinal thickness measured within the central (1 mm) ETDRS subfield.
central-subfield-thickness-max Central subfield thickness, maximumMaximum retinal thickness measured within the central (1 mm) ETDRS subfield.
macular-subfield-volume Macular ETDRS subfield volumeRetinal volume of a single ETDRS grid subfield; the subfield is identified by the component context. For the total grid volume use LOINC 57118-2.
etdrs-grid-diameters ETDRS grid circle diametersDiameters of the concentric circles of the ETDRS measurement grid used for the analysis (usually 1, 3 and 6 mm).
anatomic-reference-point Ophthalmic anatomic reference pointAnatomic structure used as the reference point to centre the measurement grid (e.g. fovea, optic disc centre).
optic-cup-area Optic cup areaArea of the optic cup from optic nerve head analysis, in mm2.
optic-cup-volume Optic cup volumeVolume of the optic cup from optic nerve head analysis, in mm3.
neuroretinal-rim-volume Neuroretinal rim volumeVolume of the neuroretinal rim from optic nerve head analysis, in mm3.
cup-disc-ratio-horizontal Cup-to-disc ratio, horizontalRatio of horizontal optic cup diameter to horizontal optic disc diameter.
cup-disc-ratio-vertical Cup-to-disc ratio, verticalRatio of vertical optic cup diameter to vertical optic disc diameter.
optic-disc-diameter-horizontal Optic disc diameter, horizontalHorizontal diameter of the optic disc, in mm.
optic-disc-diameter-vertical Optic disc diameter, verticalVertical diameter of the optic disc, in mm.
optic-disc-diameter-mean Optic disc diameter, meanMean diameter of the optic disc, in mm.
optic-cup-diameter-horizontal Optic cup diameter, horizontalHorizontal diameter of the optic cup, in mm.
optic-cup-diameter-vertical Optic cup diameter, verticalVertical diameter of the optic cup, in mm.
optic-cup-diameter-mean Optic cup diameter, meanMean diameter of the optic cup, in mm.
optic-cup-depth-mean Optic cup depth, meanMean depth of the optic cup from optic nerve head analysis, in mm.
optic-cup-depth-max Optic cup depth, maximumMaximum depth of the optic cup from optic nerve head analysis, in mm.
optic-disc-vertical-horizontal-ratio Optic disc vertical-to-horizontal diameter ratioRatio of vertical to horizontal optic disc diameter (disc ovality).
optic-cup-vertical-horizontal-ratio Optic cup vertical-to-horizontal diameter ratioRatio of vertical to horizontal optic cup diameter.
rim-disc-area-ratio Neuroretinal rim-to-disc area ratioRatio of neuroretinal rim area to optic disc area.
neuroretinal-rim-absence-extent Angular extent of neuroretinal rim absenceAngular (circumferential) extent, in degrees, over which the neuroretinal rim is absent; input to DDLS staging.
disc-damage-likelihood-scale Disc Damage Likelihood Scale (DDLS) stageDisc Damage Likelihood Scale stage (1-10), based on the narrowest rim width or angular extent of rim absence, adjusted for disc size.
rnfl-symmetry RNFL inter-eye symmetrySymmetry of the RNFL thickness profile between right and left eyes (e.g. Cirrus RNFL symmetry).
rnfl-thickness-mean-tsnit Mean RNFL thickness (TSNIT average)Average peripapillary RNFL thickness across the temporal-superior-nasal-inferior-temporal (TSNIT) profile, laterality-neutral. Instances may add an eye-specific LOINC as an optional second coding (candidates 86301-9 right / 86290-4 left, to be verified).
rnfl-thickness-tsnit-sd RNFL TSNIT profile standard deviationStandard deviation of peripapillary RNFL thickness across the TSNIT profile.
visual-field-static-perimetry Automated static perimetry (visual field)Panel code for an automated static threshold perimetry exam (e.g. Humphrey Field Analyzer).
visual-field-test-pattern Visual field test patternPattern of tested points (e.g. 24-2, 30-2, 10-2, Esterman).
visual-field-mean-deviation Visual field mean deviation (MD)Weighted average deviation of measured threshold sensitivity from age-corrected normal values, in dB.
visual-field-pattern-standard-deviation Visual field pattern standard deviation (PSD)Index of localized sensitivity loss (non-uniformity of the deviation from normal), in dB.
visual-field-index Visual field index (VFI)Global index of visual function expressed as a percentage of age-normal field.
visual-field-screening-mode Visual field screening test modeType of screening test mode used.
visual-field-fixation-strategy Visual field fixation strategyMethod used to monitor patient fixation (e.g. blind spot monitoring, gaze tracking).
perimetry-stimulus-size Perimetry stimulus sizeSize of the test stimulus (e.g. Goldmann III).
perimetry-stimulus-color Perimetry stimulus colorColor of the test stimulus light.
perimetry-background-luminance Perimetry background luminanceLuminance of the perimeter bowl background (standard 31.5 asb).
perimetry-max-stimulus-luminance Perimetry maximum stimulus luminanceMaximum luminance of the test stimulus.
perimetry-stimulus-duration Perimetry stimulus presentation timePresentation time of each stimulus (standard 200 ms).
visual-field-horizontal-extent Visual field horizontal extentHorizontal extent of the tested visual field, in degrees.
visual-field-vertical-extent Visual field vertical extentVertical extent of the tested visual field, in degrees.
visual-field-shape Visual field shapeShape of the tested visual field (circle or rectangle).
foveal-sensitivity Foveal threshold sensitivityThreshold sensitivity measured at the fovea, in dB.
visual-field-test-duration Visual field test durationTotal duration of the visual field test.
visual-field-test-point-count Number of visual field test pointsTotal number of points tested; depends on the test pattern.
correction-lens-power Correction lens powerSpherical power of the trial/correction lens used during the test, in diopters.
fixating-eye Fixating eyeThe eye that was fixating the target during the measurement. Answer is the eye (e.g. SNOMED CT 24028007 Right / 7771000 Left).
strabismus-exam Strabismus examinationPanel code for a strabismus examination grouping whichever sub-tests were performed (cover test, motility, near point of convergence, stereopsis, prism cover test, Krimsky, etc.) via hasMember.
cover-test Cover testCover test (cover-uncover and/or alternate cover) assessing the presence and type of manifest or latent ocular deviation.
ocular-motility Ocular motility assessmentAssessment of extraocular muscle function (e.g. hypofunction or hyperfunction) of a specific muscle of one eye.
near-point-of-convergence Near point of convergenceNear point of convergence (PPC), recorded as a distance in centimetres or as a qualitative finding.
convergence-assessment Convergence assessmentQualitative assessment of convergence ability (e.g. good, fair, insufficient, poor).
stereopsis-test Stereopsis testStereoacuity test result (e.g. Titmus, Randot), qualitative or in seconds of arc.
prism-cover-test Prism cover testPanel code for a prism cover test measuring ocular deviation in prism diopters across one or more gaze positions.
krimsky-test Krimsky testPanel code for a Krimsky test (corneal light reflex centred with prisms) measuring ocular deviation in prism diopters across one or more gaze positions.
hirschberg-test Hirschberg testPanel code for a Hirschberg corneal light reflex test estimating the angle of deviation across one or more gaze positions.
red-filter-light-test Red filter plus light testPanel code for a red filter plus light test assessing fusion, suppression or diplopia across one or more gaze positions.
worth-4-dot-test Worth 4 dot testPanel code for a Worth 4 dot test assessing fusion, suppression or diplopia across one or more gaze positions.
gaze-position-measurement Gaze position measurementA single measurement or finding taken at one gaze position (e.g. primary position, right gaze) within a prism cover, Krimsky, Hirschberg, red filter or Worth 4 dot test.
extraocular-muscle Extraocular muscle assessedThe extraocular muscle being assessed (one of the four rectus or two oblique muscles). Answer is a CodeableConcept naming the muscle.
extraocular-muscle-function Extraocular muscle functionFunctional finding for the assessed extraocular muscle (e.g. normal, hypofunction, hyperfunction).
stereopsis-test-type Stereopsis test typeWhich stereoacuity test was used (e.g. Titmus fly, Randot, Lang, TNO); affects interpretation of the result.
horizontal-deviation Horizontal ocular deviationMagnitude of the horizontal ocular deviation at a gaze position, always a positive magnitude, in prism diopters (or degrees for a Hirschberg estimate); the direction (eso/exo) is recorded separately.
vertical-deviation Vertical ocular deviationMagnitude of the vertical ocular deviation at a gaze position, always a positive magnitude, in prism diopters; the direction (hyper/hypo) is recorded separately.
gaze-position Gaze positionThe gaze position (direction of gaze) at which a strabismus measurement was taken, e.g. primary position, right gaze, up-and-right gaze.
gaze-position-finding Finding at gaze positionQualitative finding at a gaze position (e.g. Hirschberg reflex displacement, fusion, suppression or diplopia on red filter or Worth 4 dot testing).
within-normal-limits Within normal limitsThe measurement or analysis falls within the normal range of the device normative (age-matched reference) database (typically p >= 5%).
borderline BorderlineThe measurement or analysis falls in the borderline range of the device normative database (typically 1% <= p < 5%).
outside-normal-limits Outside normal limitsThe measurement or analysis falls outside the normal range of the device normative database (typically p < 1%).
rnfl-thickness-superior RNFL average thickness, superior quadrantAverage peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in the superior quadrant of the circumpapillary scan.
rnfl-thickness-inferior RNFL average thickness, inferior quadrantAverage peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in the inferior quadrant of the circumpapillary scan.
rnfl-thickness-nasal RNFL average thickness, nasal quadrantAverage peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in the nasal quadrant of the circumpapillary scan.
rnfl-thickness-temporal RNFL average thickness, temporal quadrantAverage peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in the temporal quadrant of the circumpapillary scan.
glaucoma-hemifield-test Glaucoma Hemifield Test resultResult of the Glaucoma Hemifield Test, comparing mirror-image superior and inferior sectors of the visual field (within normal limits, borderline, outside normal limits, general reduction of sensitivity, abnormally high sensitivity).
fixation-losses Fixation lossesNumber of fixation losses (responses to stimuli presented in the physiological blind spot) relative to the number of fixation checks performed.
false-positive-errors False positive errorsPercentage of false positive responses (responses without a stimulus being presented); a reliability index of the visual field test.
false-negative-errors False negative errorsPercentage of false negative responses (no response to a supra-threshold stimulus at a previously seen location); a reliability index of the visual field test.
test-distance-category Testing distance category (near/far)Categorical testing distance (near or far) at which a strabismus or binocular vision test was performed. Answer is a CodeableConcept (near / far). Distinct from test-distance, which records the testing distance as a Quantity.
near NearNear testing distance, approximately 33-40 cm.
far FarFar (distance) testing distance, approximately 6 m (20 ft).
horizontal-deviation-direction Horizontal deviation directionDirection of the horizontal ocular deviation at a gaze position (esodeviation, exodeviation, or orthophoria when no horizontal deviation is present). The magnitude is recorded separately as a positive value in horizontal-deviation.
vertical-deviation-direction Vertical deviation directionDirection of the vertical ocular deviation of the deviating eye at a gaze position (hyperdeviation or hypodeviation). The magnitude is recorded separately as a positive value in vertical-deviation.
esodeviation EsodeviationInward (nasal) horizontal deviation of the eye; covers esotropia and esophoria.
exodeviation ExodeviationOutward (temporal) horizontal deviation of the eye; covers exotropia and exophoria.
orthophoria OrthophoriaAbsence of any manifest or latent ocular deviation; the visual axes remain aligned under cover testing.
hyperdeviation HyperdeviationUpward vertical deviation of the deviating eye relative to the fellow eye; covers hypertropia and hyperphoria.
hypodeviation HypodeviationDownward vertical deviation of the deviating eye relative to the fellow eye; covers hypotropia and hypophoria.
fusion FusionSensory fusion: the images of both eyes are combined into a single percept (e.g. a single pinkish light on the red filter plus light test, four lights on the Worth 4 dot test). SNOMED CT 78513008 Fusion binocular vision is an observable entity, not a finding, so it is not used as an answer.
corneal-reflex-centered Corneal light reflex centeredOn corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex is centered on the pupil of the eye assessed, consistent with no manifest deviation of that eye.
corneal-reflex-displaced-nasal Corneal light reflex displaced nasallyOn corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced nasally from the pupil centre, indicating an exodeviation of that eye.
corneal-reflex-displaced-temporal Corneal light reflex displaced temporallyOn corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced temporally from the pupil centre, indicating an esodeviation of that eye.
corneal-reflex-displaced-superior Corneal light reflex displaced superiorlyOn corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced superiorly from the pupil centre, indicating a hypodeviation of that eye.
corneal-reflex-displaced-inferior Corneal light reflex displaced inferiorlyOn corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced inferiorly from the pupil centre, indicating a hyperdeviation of that eye.

name: FHIR4EyesCS
title: FHIR4Eyes Code System
description:
Local, laterality-neutral codes for ophthalmic observations and components
defined by FHIR4Eyes where no suitable side-neutral LOINC or SNOMED CT code has been
verified. Open to replacement as external codes become available.

concept.definition: Central corneal thickness, independent of the eye measured. Eye-specific LOINC: 79825-6 (right) / 79826-4 (left).
Panel code for a corneal endothelial specular microscopy exam.
Location of the corneal capture (central, paracentral, peripheral).
Type of analysis method. Eye-specific LOINC: 100086-8 (right) / 100155-1 (left).
Eye-specific LOINC: 100070-2 (right) / 100071-0 (left).
Eye-specific LOINC: 100076-9 (right) / 100077-7 (left).

concept.display: Corneal endothelial cell area coefficient of variation
concept.definition: Eye-specific LOINC: 100072-8 (right) / 100073-6 (left).
Eye-specific LOINC: 100074-4 (right) / 100075-1 (left).
Eye-specific LOINC: 100078-5 (right) / 100079-3 (left).
Eye-specific LOINC: 100080-1 (right) / 100081-9 (left).
Eye-specific LOINC: 100082-7 (right) / 100083-5 (left).

concept.display: Corneal endothelial cell area, standard deviation
concept.definition: Eye-specific LOINC: 100084-3 (right) / 100085-0 (left).
Anteroposterior length of the eye (corneal vertex to retina/RPE), e.g. by optical or ultrasound biometry.
Distance from the cornea to the anterior lens surface.
Axial thickness of the crystalline lens.
Horizontal visible corneal diameter (limbus to limbus).
Corneal power of the flattest meridian of the anterior corneal surface, in dioptres.
Corneal power of the steepest meridian of the anterior corneal surface, in dioptres.
Radius of curvature of the flattest meridian of the anterior corneal surface, in millimetres.
Radius of curvature of the steepest meridian of the anterior corneal surface, in millimetres.
Corneal (keratometric) astigmatism, the difference between steep and flat meridian powers (K2 - K1) in dioptres, reported as a positive magnitude (plus-cylinder notation) at the steep meridian.
Refractive index used to convert corneal radius of curvature into corneal power (e.g. 1.3375).
Diameter of the pupil at the time of the measurement.
Whether the pupil was pharmacologically dilated at the time of the measurement.
Mydriatic agent used to dilate the pupil, if any.
Distance between the patient and the test target (chart, fixation target) during the test, as a measured quantity. For a near/far category use test-distance-category.
Whether the test was performed with or without the patient's refractive correction.
Panel code for an ocular biometry exam (optical or ultrasound), typically for IOL power calculation. Formula results are separate IOL formula result observations.
Technique used to measure axial length: optical, ultrasound immersion or ultrasound contact.
Signal-to-noise ratio of the optical axial length measurement, a quality indicator.
Method used to select the reported axial length from multiple measurements.
Reference surfaces used for the ACD measurement (corneal epithelium or endothelium to anterior lens).
Status of the crystalline lens: phakic, pseudophakic or aphakic.
Status of the vitreous body, relevant to the sound velocity used in ultrasound biometry.
Mean radius of curvature of the anterior corneal surface in mm, (K1 radius + K2 radius)/2, as reported in the R part of the biometer R/SE field. The dioptric mean (SE) is keratometry-km.
Prior corneal or refractive surgery of the eye, critical for IOL formula selection.
Desired postoperative refraction used for IOL power calculation.
Type of refractive error of the eye.
Origin of the biometry measurement data (e.g. automatic, manually entered, from another device).
Distance between the back surface of a spectacle lens and the corneal apex.
Panel code for the result of one IOL power calculation formula applied to an ocular biometry exam.
Formula used for the IOL power calculation (e.g. Barrett Universal II, SRK/T, Holladay 2, Kane).
Type of IOL optimization constant (e.g. A-constant, surgeon factor, ACD constant).
Value of the IOL optimization constant used for the calculation.
Intraocular lens model suggested by this formula calculation.
IOL power, in dioptres, recommended by this formula calculation.
Refraction predicted by the formula for the recommended IOL power.
Range of IOL powers with the predicted refraction for each, as listed in the biometry report for this formula.
Notation in which the visual acuity value is expressed (e.g. Snellen fraction, decimal, LogMAR).
Whether the visual acuity measurement was taken through a pinhole occluder.

concept.display: Intraocular pressure corrected for central corneal thickness
concept.definition: Intraocular pressure adjusted for central corneal thickness, derived from an IOP reading and a pachymetry measurement. LOINC 96093-0/96092-2 (compensated IOP) exist but may not be equivalent to CCT-based correction; not used.
Panel grouping several intraocular pressure readings taken across a single day (diurnal / ambulatory tension curve).
Anterior corneal surface analysis component of a corneal tomography exam.
Maximum keratometric power on the anterior corneal surface; key parameter for keratoconus detection and progression.
Simulated keratometry values (steep/flat) derived from the topographic/tomographic map.
Corneal radius of curvature along the horizontal (0-180 degree) meridian; not necessarily a principal (K1/K2) meridian.
Corneal radius of curvature along the vertical (90 degree) meridian; not necessarily a principal (K1/K2) meridian.
Asphericity (Q-value) of the anterior corneal surface; typical normal value about -0.26.

concept.display: Corneal elevation relative to best fit sphere, anterior surface
concept.definition: Elevation of the anterior corneal surface relative to its best fit sphere.

concept.display: Best fit sphere radius, anterior surface
concept.definition: Radius of the best fit sphere of the anterior corneal surface.
Topographic index of local corneal surface regularity within the central zone.
Topographic index of corneal power asymmetry between opposite hemimeridians.
Difference in mean corneal power between inferior and superior regions; keratoconus screening value.
KISA% keratoconus screening index combining central K, I-S value, astigmatism and skewed radial axis.
Classification of the corneal topographic map pattern (regular, irregular, keratoconus, pellucid, post-LASIK, forme fruste).
Total corneal refractive power calculated by ray tracing through anterior and posterior corneal surfaces.
True net corneal power calculated from anterior and posterior corneal curvature using Gaussian optics.
Holladay equivalent keratometry reading over a 1.0 mm zone.
Holladay equivalent keratometry reading over a 3.0 mm zone.
Holladay equivalent keratometry reading over a 4.5 mm zone; used for IOL calculation after refractive surgery.
Mean corneal power within the central 3 mm zone.
Corneal astigmatism power within the central 3 mm zone.
Steep meridian axis within the central 3 mm zone.
Flat meridian axis within the central 3 mm zone.
Mean corneal power within the central 5 mm zone.
Corneal astigmatism power within the central 5 mm zone.
Steep meridian axis within the central 5 mm zone.
Flat meridian axis within the central 5 mm zone.
Total corneal astigmatism including the posterior surface, derived from corneal wavefront analysis.
Higher-order (irregular) component of total corneal astigmatism.
Root mean square of corneal higher-order wavefront aberrations.
Angle between the visual axis and the pupillary axis.
Coordinates (x,y) of the angle kappa intercept relative to the pupil centre.
Expected corneal astigmatism induced by the surgical incision, used in surgical planning.
Expected residual corneal astigmatism after surgery, used in toric IOL planning.
Recommended implantation axis for a toric intraocular lens.
Position coordinates of the corneal vertex.
X-coordinate of the pupil centre.
Y-coordinate of the pupil centre.
Radius of the equivalent circular pupil.
Type of topographic map encoded (axial, tangential, elevation, refractive, pachymetry).
Total area of the cornea analyzed.
Corneal eccentricity (shape factor).
Corneal keratoconus prediction index, distinct from KISA%.
Estimated potential visual acuity (decimal) from the corneal surface.
Posterior corneal surface analysis component of a corneal tomography exam.
Keratometric power of the flattest meridian of the posterior corneal surface; a negative value in dioptres.
Keratometric power of the steepest meridian of the posterior corneal surface; a negative value in dioptres.
Mean keratometric power of the posterior corneal surface; a negative value in dioptres.
Astigmatism of the posterior corneal surface, reported as a positive magnitude in dioptres (difference between posterior K2 and K1) with the posterior steep meridian as axis.
Asphericity (Q-value) of the posterior corneal surface.

concept.display: Corneal elevation relative to best fit sphere, posterior surface
concept.definition: Elevation of the posterior corneal surface relative to its best fit sphere.

concept.display: Best fit sphere radius, posterior surface
concept.definition: Radius of the best fit sphere of the posterior corneal surface.
Pachymetry (corneal thickness map) component of a corneal tomography exam.
Corneal thickness measured at the pupil centre; may differ from the thickness at the corneal apex.
Corneal thickness at the thinnest point of the pachymetry map.
Location (x,y) of the thinnest corneal point relative to the reference centre.
Total corneal volume within the analysed diameter.
Anterior chamber analysis component of a corneal tomography exam.
Volume of the anterior chamber.
Iridocorneal (anterior chamber) angle width in degrees, as measured by the tomographer.
Keratoconus screening and classification indices component of a corneal tomography exam.
Final overall deviation index (D) of the Belin-Ambrosio Enhanced Ectasia Display; key keratoconus screening index.
Deviation of anterior elevation relative to the enhanced best fit sphere (BAD component Df).
Deviation of posterior elevation relative to the enhanced best fit sphere (BAD component Db).
Deviation of the thinnest corneal thickness from normal (BAD component Dt).
Deviation of the Y-coordinate (vertical displacement) of the thinnest point (BAD component Dy).
Classification of the Belin-Ambrosio display result (normal, suspicious, abnormal).

concept.display: Enhanced best fit sphere radius, anterior surface
concept.definition: Radius of the enhanced best fit sphere of the anterior corneal surface (BAD enhanced reference).

concept.display: Enhanced best fit sphere radius, posterior surface
concept.definition: Radius of the enhanced best fit sphere of the posterior corneal surface (BAD enhanced reference).
Classic Amsler-Krumeich keratoconus staging (I-IV).
Belin ABCD keratoconus grading (anterior and posterior radius of curvature, thinnest pachymetry, distance visual acuity).
Topometric index of the deviation of individual corneal radii from the mean.
Topometric index of superior-inferior corneal curvature asymmetry.
Topometric ratio of central to peripheral corneal curvature.
Topometric central corneal curvature index.
Topometric index of superior-inferior corneal elevation asymmetry.
Topometric index of the degree of vertical decentration of corneal elevation.
Automated topographic keratoconus classification provided by the tomographer.
Corneal densitometry (light backscatter) component of a corneal tomography exam.
Corneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) in the central 0-2 mm annular zone.
Corneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) in the paracentral 2-6 mm annular zone.
Corneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) in the peripheral 6-10 mm annular zone.
Overall corneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units).
Corneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) of the anterior 120 um layer.
Corneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) of the central stromal layer.
Corneal light backscatter (densitometry, grayscale units) of the posterior 60 um layer.
Orientation of the flat meridian.
Orientation of the steep meridian.
Mean keratometry, (K1+K2)/2.
Rate of corneal thickness increase from the thinnest point toward the periphery; the pachymetric progression deviation (Dp) of the Belin-Ambrosio display.
Radius of curvature at the steepest point of the corneal surface.
Minimum radius of sagittal (axial) curvature, i.e. the steepest point of the sagittal curvature map (Pentacam topometric index Rmin).
Device-reported scan signal strength or quality score.
Boundaries used to define a retinal or RNFL thickness measurement (e.g. ILM to RPE, ILM to Bruch's membrane, ILM to RNFL outer boundary).
Classification of a measurement against the device normative database (e.g. within normal limits, borderline, outside normal limits).
Degree of pupil dilation, expressed as pupil diameter in mm.
Minimum retinal thickness measured within the central (1 mm) ETDRS subfield.
Maximum retinal thickness measured within the central (1 mm) ETDRS subfield.
Retinal volume of a single ETDRS grid subfield; the subfield is identified by the component context. For the total grid volume use LOINC 57118-2.
Diameters of the concentric circles of the ETDRS measurement grid used for the analysis (usually 1, 3 and 6 mm).
Anatomic structure used as the reference point to centre the measurement grid (e.g. fovea, optic disc centre).
Area of the optic cup from optic nerve head analysis, in mm2.
Volume of the optic cup from optic nerve head analysis, in mm3.
Volume of the neuroretinal rim from optic nerve head analysis, in mm3.
Ratio of horizontal optic cup diameter to horizontal optic disc diameter.
Ratio of vertical optic cup diameter to vertical optic disc diameter.
Horizontal diameter of the optic disc, in mm.
Vertical diameter of the optic disc, in mm.
Mean diameter of the optic disc, in mm.
Horizontal diameter of the optic cup, in mm.
Vertical diameter of the optic cup, in mm.
Mean diameter of the optic cup, in mm.
Mean depth of the optic cup from optic nerve head analysis, in mm.
Maximum depth of the optic cup from optic nerve head analysis, in mm.
Ratio of vertical to horizontal optic disc diameter (disc ovality).
Ratio of vertical to horizontal optic cup diameter.
Ratio of neuroretinal rim area to optic disc area.

concept.display: Angular extent of neuroretinal rim absence
concept.definition: Angular (circumferential) extent, in degrees, over which the neuroretinal rim is absent; input to DDLS staging.
Disc Damage Likelihood Scale stage (1-10), based on the narrowest rim width or angular extent of rim absence, adjusted for disc size.
Symmetry of the RNFL thickness profile between right and left eyes (e.g. Cirrus RNFL symmetry).

Average peripapillary RNFL thickness across the temporal-superior-nasal-inferior-temporal (TSNIT) profile, laterality-neutral. Instances may add an eye-specific LOINC as an optional second coding (candidates 86301-9 right / 86290-4 left, to be verified).
Standard deviation of peripapillary RNFL thickness across the TSNIT profile.
Panel code for an automated static threshold perimetry exam (e.g. Humphrey Field Analyzer).
Pattern of tested points (e.g. 24-2, 30-2, 10-2, Esterman).
Weighted average deviation of measured threshold sensitivity from age-corrected normal values, in dB.
Index of localized sensitivity loss (non-uniformity of the deviation from normal), in dB.
Global index of visual function expressed as a percentage of age-normal field.
Type of screening test mode used.
Method used to monitor patient fixation (e.g. blind spot monitoring, gaze tracking).
Size of the test stimulus (e.g. Goldmann III).
Color of the test stimulus light.
Luminance of the perimeter bowl background (standard 31.5 asb).
Maximum luminance of the test stimulus.
Presentation time of each stimulus (standard 200 ms).
Horizontal extent of the tested visual field, in degrees.
Vertical extent of the tested visual field, in degrees.
Shape of the tested visual field (circle or rectangle).
Threshold sensitivity measured at the fovea, in dB.
Total duration of the visual field test.

concept.display: Number of visual field test points
concept.definition: Total number of points tested; depends on the test pattern.
Spherical power of the trial/correction lens used during the test, in diopters.
The eye that was fixating the target during the measurement. Answer is the eye (e.g. SNOMED CT 24028007 Right / 7771000 Left).
Panel code for a strabismus examination grouping whichever sub-tests were performed (cover test, motility, near point of convergence, stereopsis, prism cover test, Krimsky, etc.) via hasMember.
Cover test (cover-uncover and/or alternate cover) assessing the presence and type of manifest or latent ocular deviation.
Assessment of extraocular muscle function (e.g. hypofunction or hyperfunction) of a specific muscle of one eye.
Near point of convergence (PPC), recorded as a distance in centimetres or as a qualitative finding.
Qualitative assessment of convergence ability (e.g. good, fair, insufficient, poor).
Stereoacuity test result (e.g. Titmus, Randot), qualitative or in seconds of arc.
Panel code for a prism cover test measuring ocular deviation in prism diopters across one or more gaze positions.
Panel code for a Krimsky test (corneal light reflex centred with prisms) measuring ocular deviation in prism diopters across one or more gaze positions.
Panel code for a Hirschberg corneal light reflex test estimating the angle of deviation across one or more gaze positions.
Panel code for a red filter plus light test assessing fusion, suppression or diplopia across one or more gaze positions.
Panel code for a Worth 4 dot test assessing fusion, suppression or diplopia across one or more gaze positions.
A single measurement or finding taken at one gaze position (e.g. primary position, right gaze) within a prism cover, Krimsky, Hirschberg, red filter or Worth 4 dot test.
The extraocular muscle being assessed (one of the four rectus or two oblique muscles). Answer is a CodeableConcept naming the muscle.
Functional finding for the assessed extraocular muscle (e.g. normal, hypofunction, hyperfunction).
Which stereoacuity test was used (e.g. Titmus fly, Randot, Lang, TNO); affects interpretation of the result.
Magnitude of the horizontal ocular deviation at a gaze position, always a positive magnitude, in prism diopters (or degrees for a Hirschberg estimate); the direction (eso/exo) is recorded separately.
Magnitude of the vertical ocular deviation at a gaze position, always a positive magnitude, in prism diopters; the direction (hyper/hypo) is recorded separately.
The gaze position (direction of gaze) at which a strabismus measurement was taken, e.g. primary position, right gaze, up-and-right gaze.
Qualitative finding at a gaze position (e.g. Hirschberg reflex displacement, fusion, suppression or diplopia on red filter or Worth 4 dot testing).
The measurement or analysis falls within the normal range of the device normative (age-matched reference) database (typically p >= 5%).
The measurement or analysis falls in the borderline range of the device normative database (typically 1% <= p < 5%).
The measurement or analysis falls outside the normal range of the device normative database (typically p < 1%).
Average peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in the superior quadrant of the circumpapillary scan.
Average peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in the inferior quadrant of the circumpapillary scan.
Average peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in the nasal quadrant of the circumpapillary scan.
Average peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in the temporal quadrant of the circumpapillary scan.

Result of the Glaucoma Hemifield Test, comparing mirror-image superior and inferior sectors of the visual field (within normal limits, borderline, outside normal limits, general reduction of sensitivity, abnormally high sensitivity).
Number of fixation losses (responses to stimuli presented in the physiological blind spot) relative to the number of fixation checks performed.
Percentage of false positive responses (responses without a stimulus being presented); a reliability index of the visual field test.
Percentage of false negative responses (no response to a supra-threshold stimulus at a previously seen location); a reliability index of the visual field test.

Categorical testing distance (near or far) at which a strabismus or binocular vision test was performed. Answer is a CodeableConcept (near / far). Distinct from test-distance, which records the testing distance as a Quantity.
Near testing distance, approximately 33-40 cm.
Far (distance) testing distance, approximately 6 m (20 ft).

Direction of the horizontal ocular deviation at a gaze position (esodeviation, exodeviation, or orthophoria when no horizontal deviation is present). The magnitude is recorded separately as a positive value in horizontal-deviation.
Direction of the vertical ocular deviation of the deviating eye at a gaze position (hyperdeviation or hypodeviation). The magnitude is recorded separately as a positive value in vertical-deviation.
Inward (nasal) horizontal deviation of the eye; covers esotropia and esophoria.
Outward (temporal) horizontal deviation of the eye; covers exotropia and exophoria.
Absence of any manifest or latent ocular deviation; the visual axes remain aligned under cover testing.
Upward vertical deviation of the deviating eye relative to the fellow eye; covers hypertropia and hyperphoria.
Downward vertical deviation of the deviating eye relative to the fellow eye; covers hypotropia and hypophoria.

Sensory fusion: the images of both eyes are combined into a single percept (e.g. a single pinkish light on the red filter plus light test, four lights on the Worth 4 dot test). SNOMED CT 78513008 Fusion binocular vision is an observable entity, not a finding, so it is not used as an answer.
On corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex is centered on the pupil of the eye assessed, consistent with no manifest deviation of that eye.
On corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced nasally from the pupil centre, indicating an exodeviation of that eye.
On corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced temporally from the pupil centre, indicating an esodeviation of that eye.
On corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced superiorly from the pupil centre, indicating a hypodeviation of that eye.
On corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced inferiorly from the pupil centre, indicating a hyperdeviation of that eye.
